src.imagery: Esri World Imagery through its Wayback archive – five dated pictures of the same ground, read at web-mercator zoom 19 (0.209 m a pixel; the 2011 aerial only exists at zoom 18, 0.418 m). Looked at and measured only.

pictures.name: e2025

pictures.name: a2011
pictures.use: the FRAME of this file; cross-check, warp, marks

src.better_imagery_not_reached: Regione Lombardia orthophoto (AGEA 2021, 20 cm): the public server (www.cartografia.servizirl.it) does not answer from this Mac nor from the web-fetch tool. The national geoportal only has 2012 at 50 cm.

frame.what: the [lat, lon] here are in the frame of the 2011 AERIAL picture (the best stated accuracy of the five, 2.72 m; it lies near the middle of the five; OpenStreetMap's pit building outline fits its roof). They are NOT in the frame of today's Esri World Imagery (the 2025 satellite picture), which lies about 3 m south of it.

to_draw_on_todays_esri_picture.move_each_point_by_m: east = -0.574 -0.000476·x − (+0.000622)·y, north = -2.999 + (+0.000622)·x -0.000476·y, with x / y = metres east / north of the middle
to_draw_on_todays_esri_picture.then: that picture is also warped locally by ±0.4 m (16–84 %), up to 1.5 m by underpasses and through the Ascari chicane, and lies about 0.9 m further ALONG the main straight

src.method: the track straightened along its own middle (one row a metre, 0.1 m across) in each picture; each white line followed round the lap as the best smooth path of the step from tarmac up to the line (brightness in logarithm, so a line in a tree's shadow counts); then, row by row, a blurred three-level model (tarmac | line 0.20 m wide | ground outside) fitted across the line, which gives the line's OUTER side whether the line stands on dark ground (a ridge) or against a kerb or gravel (a step). The edges given are the ones the 2025 picture shows (the only picture after the 2024 resurfacing), with that picture's own local warp taken out: the warp moves both edges together and is read from the four earlier pictures, only where they show both lines and the same width as 2025 (or two of them agree with each other). All conversions between lat / lon and metres use a transverse Mercator projection of the WGS84 ellipsoid through the circuit's centre (Krüger series), no fixed metres-per-degree constant.

warp_reading.why: trees over the Serraglio straight (the earlier pictures are displaced or dark there), the old banking's bridge, the Ascari entry

line_not_seen.what: sections [from, to, metres] where no picture shows the line (bridge, tree crown, a broken line) and the edge is carried straight across from either side

src.changed_since_the_earlier_pictures: where the 2025 lines differ from the earlier pictures by more than the measurement: the first chicane (the white lines now run up to about 5 m further out round both bends; the apex kerbs stand where they stood); the main straight's right line 0.5 m further out than in 2011 (as in 2020); Lesmo 1 left edge about 0.7 m further out; the entry of the Parabolica left edge 0.2 … 0.5 m further out; the grid boxes 0.9 m nearer the start line. Over the lap the two lines are 0.1 … 0.2 m further apart in 2025 than before (median).

against_monza_pitlane_json.what: carpilot/venue/stands/monza_pitlane.json was read on today's Esri picture (the 2025 one) and tied to the map's door line; this file is in the 2011 aerial's frame. Compared only, not edited.
against_monza_pitlane_json.reading_against_reading_in_the_2025_pict: track right edge, mine − theirs (+ = further from the pit building): +0.71 m (u −171), −0.08 (−133), +0.57 (−97), +0.47 (−62), +0.44 (−28), −0.05 (0), −0.06 (120), +0.51 (300), +0.18 (361), −0.11 (416), −0.26 (470), +0.20 (503); left edge +0.29 / +0.21 / +0.08 m (u 0 / 300 / 400); width 12.4 m (theirs 12.3); start line u 298.9 (theirs 299.4), finish line u −10.8 (theirs −11.2); pit exit line within 0.33 m at their four points, leaving the right line at u 416.5 (theirs 416) and ending at u 799; broken right line u 421 … 478 (theirs 416 … 480); pit entry broken line u −235 … −173 (theirs −229 … −171). No difference over 0.7 m: no sign of a shadow taken for the track's line on this straight. The pit wall and the lane's own lines were not measured again.
against_monza_pitlane_json.frames: a point read on today's Esri picture goes into this file's frame by about u +2.0 m (further along) and v +0.5 … +0.9 m (towards the track) on the pit straight (east −0.6 … +0.1, north +2.9 … +3.3 m, less 0.9 m along the straight). Until one of the two is moved, the lane's lines and this file's edges are that far apart.

src.stations: section i lies s_m[i] m along the lap from section 0 (list "s_m"); section 0 is 1.0 m before the finish line

marks_note.start: the start line, its ends on the two edges. Read at stations 310.25 (2011), 310.8 (2020), 310.6 (2022) and 311.55 (2025, which lies 0.9 m further along this straight – the finish line shows the same): 310.6 m after section 0.
marks_note.control: the finish (control) line – the thick line across track and pit lane, 16 m after the big gantry: 0.7 m after section 0; 309.6 m before the start line (the published offset is 309 m).
marks_note.pole: the front line of pole's grid box as painted now: on the LEFT of the track (in every picture, 2011–2025), 2.25 m behind the start line (it was 2.8 … 3.5 m before the 2024 resurfacing); the second box is on the right, 8 m further back. Its place across the track (2.5 m wide, 2.2 … 4.7 m in from the left edge) is from the 2020 picture: the 2025 picture shows the line smeared over the whole left half.

pit_entry.with: monza_pitlane.json entry: the track's own right line is BROKEN here (dashes) where the entry lane leaves; the edge given is that broken line carried straight. The safety car line 1 crosses the track at its end (section 873).

pit_exit.edge_is: the track's OWN right line all the way: broken (dashes) over sections 47–58 where the exit lane crosses it – carried straight – and solid again after.

pit_exit_line.what: the solid line between the exit lane and the track (monza_pitlane.json exit.left, "A"). It leaves the track's right line at section 46 and then runs INSIDE the track's width, 3.2 … 4.2 m from the right line, to where it simply ends (no line across) 9.1 m after section 90. Its points at sections 46 … 90 (the same sections as edges.right), outer = lane side.

pit_exit.why_not_the_edge: if this line were taken as the track's edge (as at Zandvoort, where the lane lies beside the track), the main straight would be 6.6 m wide for 383 m and the right-hand grid column would launch outside the track. To use it as the edge all the same: replace edges.right[46 … 90] by pit_exit_line.line (the lane's far side is then the old edges.right there).
pit_exit.lane_far_side: over sections 47–58 the lane's far (pit) side is monza_pitlane.json exit.right ("B"), which meets the track's right line at the end of the broken stretch; from there to the line's end the lane is the strip between pit_exit_line and edges.right
